advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Mirror the CLI's new ConfigError boundary onto the MCP write adapter: teach _mcp_errors._envelope_error to wrap ConfigError into a structured error envelope so unreadable-config faults on transition_ticket/claim_ticket are delivered like every other known rebar error.
evidence: Diff adds CLI boundary: `except ConfigError as e:` -> `sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")` in src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:267
gates.py diff: `raise ConfigError(f"cannot resolve {gate_label} for {ticket_id}: ...") from exc` — now raised out of gate_enabled through rebar.transition/rebar.claim
src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:20: `class ConfigError(ValueError):` — ConfigError is a ValueError, not a RebarError (src/rebar/_errors.py:19: `class RebarError(RuntimeError):`)

src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:56: `if isinstance(exc, (RebarError, CommandError, mismatch_type, llm_error_type)):` — ConfigError is not in this set, so _envelope_error returns None and the exception is re-raised unwrapped
src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:259 (`rebar.transition(...)`) and :289 (`rebar.claim(...)`) are the MCP write ops that now propagate ConfigError under an unreadable config
advisory.finding: The 39f8-ae7c change makes gated write ops raise ConfigError on an unreadable config, and adds a ConfigError boundary handler to the CLI write adapter (_cli/__init__.py) to render it as a clean `Error: ...` + exit 1, but the sibling MCP write adapter's structured-error boundary (_mcp_errors._envelope_error) was NOT updated to recognize ConfigError. Because ConfigError subclasses ValueError (not RebarError/CommandError/ConcurrencyMismatch/LLMError), _envelope_error returns None for it, so an unreadable config on MCP transition_ticket/claim_ticket escapes as an unstructured ToolError instead of the structured error envelope the MCP surface delivers for every other known rebar error.
scenarios: An MCP client invokes transition_ticket or claim_ticket against a repo whose rebar.toml is present but malformed while a verify.* gate would resolve; the ConfigError raised by gate_enabled is not wrapped into the structured error_envelope, so the agent cannot branch on a machine-readable error code the way it can for every other rebar error (and the way the CLI now surfaces it as a clean Error: line).
advisory.suggested_fix: In src/rebar/_mcp_errors._envelope_error, add ConfigError to the recognized-exception set — e.g. import `from rebar.config import ConfigError` and include it in the isinstance tuple at line 56 (`isinstance(exc, (RebarError, CommandError, mismatch_type, llm_error_type, ConfigError))`), with an error_code_for mapping — so an unreadable-config ConfigError raised out of gate_enabled is delivered as the structured envelope, matching the CLI boundary added in this diff.
